learningObjectives.title: Dance styles and rhythms (waltz, tango, salsa)

questions.q: In which metre (time signature) is the waltz written?
questions.explain: The waltz is in triple time (3/4), giving it its characteristic one-two-three lilt.

questions.q: The traditional Argentine tango is usually written in which metre?
questions.explain: The tango is in duple time, most commonly notated as 2/4.

questions.q: Salsa is normally felt and written in which metre?
questions.explain: Salsa is in quadruple time (4/4), over which the clave pattern is laid.

questions.q: In which country did the tango originate?
questions.explain: The tango developed in the port city of Buenos Aires, Argentina.

questions.q: Which country is most associated with the origin of the Viennese waltz?
questions.explain: The waltz became popular in the ballrooms of Vienna, Austria, in the 19th century.

questions.q: Which instrument is central to the sound of the traditional tango?
questions.explain: The bandoneón is the signature instrument that gives the tango its distinctive expressive tone.

questions.q: Which salsa instrument consists of two wooden sticks struck together?
questions.explain: Claves are two wooden sticks tapped together, often sounding the key clave rhythm.

questions.q: Which composer became known as the 'Waltz King' for his Viennese waltzes?
questions.explain: Johann Strauss II, composer of 'The Blue Danube', was nicknamed the 'Waltz King'.

questions.q: What does the characteristic 'oom-pah-pah' waltz accompaniment consist of?
options: A bass note on beat 1 with chords on beats 2 and 3
Chords played equally on all three beats
A bass note played on every beat
questions.explain: The 'oom' is a bass note on the strong first beat, and the 'pah-pah' is chords on beats 2 and 3.

questions.q: Which best describes the clave in salsa music?
options: A repeating rhythmic pattern of five strokes spread over two bars
A slow sustained melody played on strings
A single held chord at the start of each section
questions.explain: The clave is a five-stroke rhythmic pattern spanning two bars that underpins the whole salsa texture.

questions.q: Which is a characteristic feature of tango music?
options: Sharp, staccato articulation with dramatic pauses and dotted rhythms
Smooth, continuous flowing motion in triple time
Call-and-response brass over an off-beat clave
questions.explain: The tango is marked by sharp, staccato phrasing, dotted rhythms and dramatic pauses that mirror the dance.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the bandoneón?
options: A free-reed instrument (a type of concertina) central to the tango
questions.explain: The bandoneón is a free-reed, concertina-like instrument whose expressive tone defines the tango sound.

questions.q: Which best describes the origins of salsa?
options: Cuban and Puerto Rican roots, developed in New York
The port cities of Buenos Aires and Montevideo
questions.explain: Salsa grew from Cuban and Puerto Rican dance styles and was developed by Latin communities in New York.

questions.q: Compared with the slow (English) waltz, the Viennese waltz is:
questions.explain: The Viennese waltz is danced at a much faster tempo, requiring couples to rotate quickly around the floor.

questions.q: Which instruments typically form the brass section of a salsa band?
questions.explain: Salsa bands feature a bright brass section of trumpets and trombones playing riffs and fills.

questions.q: A dance requires couples to rotate quickly and continuously around the floor in fast triple time. This is most characteristic of the:
questions.explain: Fast triple time with continuous rotating movement is the hallmark of the Viennese waltz.

questions.q: You hear a piece with staccato dotted rhythms, dramatic pauses and a bandoneón leading the melody. Which dance is this?
questions.explain: Staccato dotted rhythms, dramatic pauses and the bandoneón are all defining features of the tango.

questions.q: You hear a lively piece in 4/4 with congas, claves and a brass section over a repeated piano montuno. Which dance is this?
questions.explain: The 4/4 clave-based texture with Latin percussion, brass and piano montuno identifies this as salsa.

questions.q: A student counts a steady 1-2-3, 1-2-3 while listening, feeling the music lilt around beat 1. What is the metre, and which dance does this suggest?
questions.explain: A repeating count of three with emphasis on beat 1 indicates triple time (3/4), the metre of the waltz.
